Review · How we assessed risk

Fix. This section was left as a scaffold because the wiki holds no evidence for it: no page records who did a risk assessment, against what framework, or when it was revisited. It is also the section the Safety and Security award is decided on, because it is the one that shows a method rather than a list of hazards. A person has to write it, and the empty table has to be filled with the risks the other sections already name: the culture crossing the membrane, the pump-head envelope, acetone, the electroporator, mains power beside a water loop, and the cargo slot. Name the framework used, the date of each review, and the person who signed it off.

Biological risk

Containment is a design intent

Retention has not been demonstrated in our hands, and the second containment layer has not been built. Contained use is a classification we are pursuing, not one we hold.

Chassis

B. subtilis 168, risk group, and why it was chosen. Note that it sporulates, which cuts both ways.

Payload

ACC deaminase, in the open literature since the 1990s. Say what it does and does not do in a non-target organism.

Escape

The membrane is intended to retain every cell. Intended, not demonstrated. The second containment layer does not exist yet.

Review · Biological risk

Works. Drafted overnight on 25 September 2026 from evidence already on this wiki. The three subsections are now built from Parts, Experiments, Engineering, Results and Hardware, and each claim links to the page it came from. Nothing about a risk group, a regulatory status or a containment rating is asserted anywhere.

Fix. A person has to supply the risk group of B. subtilis 168 and of E. coli DH5-alpha, with the source used, and the local rule that sets them; the draft says only that the wiki does not record one. Somebody has to state whether strain 168 sporulates under the reactor's conditions and what that means for an escaped cell, because the original scaffold note raised it and no page on this wiki answers it. The escape subsection rests on one plating with no recorded incubation conditions; say whether the team intends to repeat it before the freeze, since the whole containment argument sits on it. Check the payload paragraph against the PI's view before publishing: it says none of the three cargoes is a toxin, an antibiotic resistance determinant or a virulence factor, which is a safety claim and needs a name behind it.

Chemical and physical risk

Reagents, high-intensity LEDs, pressure in the flow path, mains power near water.

Review · Chemical and physical risk

Works. Drafted overnight on 25 September 2026 from evidence already on this wiki. Every hazard named here is one the wiki already documents, and the reagent list is taken from the protocols on Experiments rather than from a generic list.

Fix. The draft names hazards and does not assess them: each one needs an exposure route, a control and who is responsible. Acetone is the one to start with, because it is used by the millilitre and is also the classroom demonstration, and the wiki does not say what ventilation, what volume per session or what adult supervision that demonstration ran under. Confirm the DiOPAL sentence with whoever built it; the wiki describes the array but records no irradiance, so the word bright is the strongest claim the evidence supports. Add the safety data sheet reference for each reagent once they are to hand.

Security and dual use

A retaskable expression slot is the project's best feature and its security question. Answer it directly.

Review · Security and dual use

Works. Drafted overnight on 25 September 2026 from evidence already on this wiki. The argument is built from what Parts records about the cargo slot and from the position taken on Laws and Regulations.

Fix. The last paragraph deliberately stops short of a conclusion, and the team has to supply one: state whether the parts will be submitted with the slot described as retaskable, and what a Registry entry will and will not say. Check the four limiting factors with somebody who knows the host; the draft states them from the wiki's own record, not from a security assessment. If the team has discussed dual use with an advisor or with iGEM Safety, record the date and the outcome here, because an award for security work is decided on evidence of that conversation.

Containment design

What is engineered in rather than administered: membrane, enclosure, interlocks, kill conditions.

Review · Containment design

Works. Drafted overnight on 25 September 2026 from evidence already on this wiki. Built from Hardware, Measurement and Experiments. It says plainly that there is no kill switch, no auxotrophy and no second containment layer.

Fix. Experiments points at this page for the kill switch argument. Either write that argument, saying why a kill switch was not built and what would have to be true to need one, or change the sentence on Experiments so it does not promise something this page does not carry. If any of the three unbuilt safety instruments will exist before the freeze, say which and by when; if none will, say that instead, because an unbuilt instrument described in the present tense reads as a claim.

Lab practice, training and supervision

Who was trained, on what, by whom, and who was allowed to work alone. This is a high-school team; say what the supervision actually was.

Review · Lab practice, training and supervision

Works. Drafted overnight on 25 September 2026 from evidence already on this wiki. The supervision facts come from Plants and are the only ones the wiki records.

Fix. This section is mostly a gap and the gap is the important part for a high-school team: who was trained, on what, by whom, and who was allowed to work alone. That list exists only in people's heads and has to be written down, with dates. Name the host laboratory and the person responsible for the team in it. Say what personal protective equipment was required and whether it was worn, since the photographs on Plants show gloves and lab coats but no page states a rule.

Shipping, disposal and incidents

Autoclave and waste route, and what happened the one time something went wrong.

Review · Shipping, disposal and incidents

Works. Drafted overnight on 25 September 2026 from evidence already on this wiki. The two incidents are the ones the wiki already reports, and the draft says plainly that the disposal route is not documented anywhere.

Fix. Somebody has to write the actual waste route: what happens to plates, cultures, reactor fluid and acetone waste, who takes them, and under what rule. That is the single largest hole on this page and a judge will look for it. Neither incident was written up as a safety incident at the time; give each one a date, the people present and the corrective action, and say whether anything was reported to the host laboratory. If anything was shipped, including the seed from Prof. Cheng's laboratory, say so and under what permission.
